title: Praline layer cake
subtitle: four layers of almond sponge with praline buttercream and a caramel top
excerpt: Praline layer cake is a show-stopping celebration cake built from thin almond sponge layers sandwiched with praline-flavoured Swiss meringue buttercream. The crushed praline gives the buttercream a caramel crunch that contrasts with the smooth sponge. A poured caramel glaze on top adds drama. The cake takes several stages but each component can be made over two days.
sourceNotes: Praline layer cake informed by French gateau tradition; Swiss meringue buttercream method from modern British patisserie.

glossaryTerms.definition: Nuts coated in or embedded in caramelised sugar. When the sugar cools and sets, the result is either left as a brittle slab or ground to a paste used to flavour creams and buttercreams.
A smooth, stable buttercream made by cooking egg whites and sugar together to 74°C, then whipping to a meringue before beating in butter. Less sweet and more silky than American buttercream.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Sponge layers can be made 2 days ahead and wrapped. Praline can be made up to 5 days ahead in a sealed jar. Assemble on the day of serving or the day before.

baking.decoratingTechnique: praline buttercream with poured caramel top

content.text: This cake has three components: the almond sponge, the

. Each can be made separately. The praline is stirred into the finished buttercream to give it its flavour and texture. The easiest order is: praline first (it keeps for days), then the sponge, then the buttercream on the day of assembly.
Almond sponge (fills two 20 cm tins, each split to give 4 layers)

Heat 100 g caster sugar in a small dry saucepan over medium heat without stirring until it turns a deep amber caramel. Add 100 g flaked almonds, stir once to coat, then pour onto a lined baking tray. Leave to set hard (about 20 minutes), then break into pieces and crush in a food processor to coarse crumbs. Set aside.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Grease and line two 20 cm round cake tins.

Beat butter and 250 g caster sugar until pale and fluffy. Add eggs one at a time, beating well. Fold in flour, ground almonds, milk, and almond extract. Divide between the two tins and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean and the sponge springs back when pressed. Cool completely.
Split each sponge horizontally into two thin layers using a long serrated knife. You now have 4 layers.

Combine 5 egg whites and 300 g caster sugar in the bowl of a stand mixer set over a saucepan of barely simmering water. Whisk constantly by hand until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture reaches 74°C. Remove from the heat and whisk on high speed for 8 to 10 minutes until the meringue is at stiff peaks and the bowl is cool.

Switch to the paddle attachment and beat in the 400 g room-temperature butter a piece at a time on medium speed. The buttercream may look curdled before it comes together; keep beating. Once smooth, beat in the crushed praline.

Stack the four layers with praline buttercream between each one. Apply a crumb coat of buttercream all over and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Apply the final coat of buttercream and smooth. Decorate the top with additional praline shards or a poured thin caramel before serving.

attrs.avoid: Avoid adding butter before the meringue bowl is fully cool to the touch.
attrs.fix: Keep beating on medium speed for a further 3 to 5 minutes; split buttercream almost always comes back together.

attrs.problem: Sponge layers splitting or tearing when cut
attrs.avoid: Avoid cutting sponges when still warm; they must be fully cold.
attrs.fix: Use a long serrated knife in a sawing motion with minimal downward pressure.
